title: CLI/config integration and command resolution pipeline
description:
Wire session-launching flags through figment2 config loading, resolve into final CommandSpec before session startup.

## CLI parsing

New flags added to CliArgs (clap derive):
- --shell <name>
- --ssh <host>
- --mosh <host>
- --tmux <session>
- --tmux-create <session>
- --tmux-attach <session>
- --dir <path>
- --no-login (flag)
- --no-interactive (flag)

Trailing -- command args still supported as innermost layer.

## Resolution pipeline

The SessionLaunchSpec (all the flags above) resolves into CommandSpec via:

1. Determine shell (launcher-shell ticket)
2. Build tmux command if any tmux flag (launcher-tmux ticket)
3. Determine inner command: trailing args > tmux command > None
4. Build shell invocation (launcher-shell ticket)
5. Wrap in transport if ssh/mosh (launcher-transport ticket)
6. Result: CommandSpec consumed by existing retry loop

## Trailing args interaction

If trailing -- command present AND tmux flags present:
- Trailing command runs INSIDE tmux session
- inner_cmd becomes: tmux new -As <session>  # then user command runs inside via tmux default-command? 
Actually: tmux runs the shell, shell sources rc, then user's trailing command runs.
This needs careful thought during implementation.

If trailing command present WITHOUT tmux:
- inner_cmd becomes the trailing command directly
- Shell wraps: zsh -lic 'exec <trailing>'

## Config integration

New fields in Config or a separate SessionLaunchConfig struct:
- launch_shell: Option<String>
- launch_ssh: Option<String>
- launch_mosh: Option<String>
- launch_tmux: Option<TmuxMode>  (enum: CreateOrAttach/Create/Attach with session name)
- launch_dir: Option<String>
- launch_login: bool (default true)
- launch_interactive: bool (default true)

Loaded via figment2 with same precedence: CLI > env > TOML > defaults.

## Retry behavior

RetryLoop already re-runs the resolved CommandSpec. Since CommandSpec includes the full stack (ssh/mosh + shell + tmux), retry reconnects and re-attaches. No changes needed to retry loop.

## Env var support

TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_SSH=w
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_TMUX=compfuzor
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_DIR=~/src/foo
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_LOGIN=false

## Testing

Integration tests: verify resolved CommandSpec for various flag combinations. Test config file loading of launch fields. Test env var overrides.
notes:
## --dir without tmux (clarified)

When --dir is specified without tmux flags, the inner command is cd + exec shell:

  title-proxy --dir ~/src/foo
  → zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec zsh -li'

  title-proxy --ssh w --dir ~/src/foo
  → ssh w -- zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec zsh -li'

Starts an interactive shell from inside the target directory.

## --dir with trailing command but no tmux

  title-proxy --dir ~/src/foo -- make test
  → zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec make test'

title: Remote transport flags (--ssh, --mosh)
description:
Parse remote transport flags, enforce mutual exclusivity, wrap command vector in transport layer.

## Flags (mutually exclusive -- error if both specified)

- --ssh <host>: wraps command in SSH transport
- --mosh <host>: wraps command in mosh transport

## Wrapping

Given a resolved shell command vector, produce the transport-wrapped vector:
- SSH: [ssh, <host>, --, ...shell_cmd]
- mosh: [mosh, <host>, --, ...shell_cmd]
- Neither: shell_cmd (unchanged)

## Example

Shell cmd: [zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']
With --ssh w: [ssh, w, --, zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']
With --mosh w: [mosh, w, --, zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']

## --dir on remote

--dir refers to the REMOTE filesystem when ssh/mosh is active. The shell wrapping handles cd on the remote side.

## Testing

Pure unit tests. Test ssh wrapping, mosh wrapping, mutual exclusivity error, no-transport passthrough.

title: Tmux session flags and command construction
description:
Parse tmux-related flags, enforce mutual exclusivity, build tmux command strings.

## Flags (mutually exclusive -- fail if multiple specified)

- --tmux <session>: create-or-attach → tmux new -As <session>
- --tmux-create <session>: create only → tmux new -s <session>
- --tmux-attach <session>: attach only → tmux a -t <session>

## --dir integration

When --dir is specified alongside tmux:
- create-or-attach: tmux new -c <dir> -As <session>
- create: tmux new -c <dir> -s <session>
- attach: tmux attach-session -c <dir> -t <session> (tmux 3.0+)

When --dir is specified WITHOUT tmux: handled by shell layer (cd wrapping).

## Output

Produces an optional tmux command string (e.g. 'tmux new -c ~/src/foo -As dev') that becomes the inner command for the shell invocation builder.

If no tmux flags specified: None (shell runs bare or with trailing command).

## Testing

Pure unit tests. Test all three modes, --dir integration, mutual exclusivity error cases.
notes:
## Trailing command + tmux (clarified)

Trailing args become tmux's command argument natively:

  title-proxy --mosh w --tmux dev -- vim
  → mosh w -- zsh -lic 'exec tmux new -As dev vim'

tmux handles this correctly — vim runs inside the new/attached session.

title: Shell family detection and invocation builder
description:
Pure functional core: detect shell family from name/path, build shell invocation vectors.

## Shell families

| Family | Shells | Login+command | Bare login+interactive |
|--------|--------|---------------|------------------------|
| POSIX | bash, zsh, sh, dash | <shell> -lc 'exec <cmd>' | <shell> -li |
| fish | fish | fish -lc 'exec <cmd>' | fish -li |
| nushell | nu, nushell | nu -c '<cmd>' | nu |

Nushell has no -l flag and no exec builtin; nu -c exits after running.

## Shell fallback chain

1. --shell flag value (if provided)
2. $SHELL env var basename
3. zsh (if it exists on PATH)
4. sh

Detection takes the basename of the path (handles /bin/zsh, /usr/bin/zsh, zsh all mapping to zsh).

## Flags

- --shell <name>: explicit override, accepts full path or basename
- --no-login: skip -l (default: login)
- --no-interactive: skip -i (default: interactive)

## Invocation builder

Given a shell name, login/interactive booleans, and optional inner command, produce Vec<String>:
- No inner command: [shell, (-l if login), (-i if interactive)]
- With inner command (POSIX/fish): [shell, (-l), (-i), -c, 'exec <inner>']
- With inner command (nu): [nu, -c, '<inner>']

## Testing

Pure unit tests, no I/O. Test all three families, login/interactive combos, fallback chain.
notes:
## Fallback resolution (clarified)

For the no-information case (no --shell, no $SHELL), emit a portable runtime snippet rather than checking PATH locally:

- Without inner command: sh -c 'command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec zsh -li || exec sh -li'
- With inner command: sh -c 'if command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec zsh -lic "exec <inner>"; else exec sh -lc "exec <inner>"; fi'

This works locally and remotely without needing to probe the target filesystem before connecting. sh is guaranteed on any Unix; the snippet promotes to zsh at runtime if available.

The resolution chain becomes:
1. --shell flag → use directly
2. $SHELL → use directly
3. Neither → emit runtime detection snippet via sh -c
## Updated per design doc resolutions

Shell fallback now respects remote $SHELL. Updated chain:
1. --shell flag → use directly (no existence check, pass through)
2. $SHELL env var → use directly
3. Runtime snippet via sh -c that checks $SHELL on the target, then zsh, then sh:
   sh -c 'if [ -n "$SHELL" ]; then exec "$SHELL" -li; elif command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec zsh -li; else exec sh -li; fi'

No local PATH checks. The snippet runs on the target machine (local or remote).

See doc/design/2026-06-22-session-launcher.md for full pipeline architecture.

title: Session launching flags for composable remote/tmux/shell commands
description:
title-proxy currently accepts a single trailing command vector. This epic adds composable convenience flags that resolve into a single CommandSpec before session startup.

## Flags

- --shell <name>: shell override (default: $SHELL basename, fallback zsh-then-sh)
- --ssh <host>: SSH transport (mutually exclusive with --mosh)
- --mosh <host>: mosh transport (mutually exclusive with --ssh)
- --tmux <session>: create-or-attach (tmux new -As)
- --tmux-create <session>: create only (tmux new -s)
- --tmux-attach <session>: attach only (tmux a -t)
- --dir <path>: working directory for innermost layer
- --no-login: skip login shell mode
- --no-interactive: skip interactive shell mode

## Composition model

Flags build the command vector inside-out: shell (innermost) -> optional tmux wraps inside shell -> optional ssh/mosh wraps everything.

Example: title-proxy --mosh w --tmux compfuzor
Resolves to: mosh w -- zsh -lic 'exec tmux new -As compfuzor'

## Key decisions

- --tmux defaults to create-or-attach; --tmux-create/--tmux-attach are explicit; fail if multiple specified
- --ssh and --mosh mutually exclusive
- Default: login + interactive shell (-li for POSIX) for full env setup
- Shell fallback: --shell > $SHELL > zsh (if exists) > sh
- Trailing -- command runs as innermost layer
- Retry re-runs fully resolved CommandSpec (reconnects, re-attaches)
notes:
## Architecture finalized

See doc/design/2026-06-22-session-launcher.md for the full design.

Key shape: LaunchConfig nested in Config (not a standalone spec). Pure resolution pipeline in launch.rs with 4 stages: resolve_shell → resolve_inner_command → build_shell_invocation → wrap_transport.

Implementation order: tickets 1-3 (shell/tmux/transport) are all pure functions in launch.rs, can be built together. Ticket 4 (config integration) wires them to CLI/config/proxy.

tmux 3.0+ baseline (for attach-session -c). Shell pass-through, no existence check. Remote $SHELL fallback in detection snippet.
